Company experience · Enterprise AI

Barrel

Turning business workflows into an AI product people could use.

Role
Co-founder & CEO
Period
2023–2025
Focus
Workflow design & product delivery

The product challenge

At Barrel, I worked on converting HR and IT processes into actions an AI agent could execute. That required defining the actions, the rules around them, and the points at which a person needed to approve the next step.

The work connected business processes to explicit product behavior. My ownership was product and company leadership; implementation was a team effort.

From workflow to product

I led the team from concept to the first version of the product. My contribution included translating workflows into agent actions, rules, and human-approval paths, then connecting those requirements to delivery priorities.

Human approval was part of how the workflow was designed. Defining those approval points made the relationship between agent actions and human decisions explicit.

Learning with customers

I built an enterprise design-partner program that connected customer usage to product decisions. We tested HR and IT workflows and reviewed usage and failure patterns weekly. Those reviews informed changes to the roadmap and helped the team decide what to build next.

This gave customer feedback a recurring place in delivery. The practical work was connecting an observed issue or pattern with a product requirement and a decision about priorities.

Connecting product and commercial decisions

My responsibilities also included go-to-market and monetization strategy. I introduced value-based pricing and a structured pilot sales approach tailored to customer willingness to pay.

The case brings together the parts of product leadership I owned: making workflow behavior explicit, coordinating technical delivery, learning from customer usage, and connecting those lessons to commercial decisions. It reflects work delivered with a team, with my contribution centered on product and company leadership.

The through line

Business process → product behavior

  • Define the agent’s actions and limits.
  • Make human approval part of the workflow.
  • Use customer failure patterns to inform priorities.
  • Connect product learning to commercialization.
